report.source_text: Histopathology demonstrated a 75 mm grade 2 jejunal leiomyosarcoma with negative margins and one of four lymph nodes demonstrating metastatic disease. The remaining three lymph nodes showed features consistent with known lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma. Epstein-Barr virus (EBV)-encoded RNA was negative, and the possibility of an EBV-associated leiomyosarcoma was excluded.

clinician.final_diagnosis: jejunal leiomyosarcoma with metastatic lymph node involvement
clinician.trajectory_summary: An elderly man with a past small bowel mass and lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma presented with symptoms of small bowel obstruction. CT abdomen-pelvis revealed a large, enlarging obstructing distal small bowel mass. Surgical resection of the mass and lymph node sampling was performed. Histopathology confirmed a 75 mm grade 2 jejunal leiomyosarcoma with negative margins and metastatic disease in one of four lymph nodes. The patient had an uneventful recovery and was discharged on postoperative day 7.
